 CORAM: THE HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAVI V.HOSMANI  -2-  NC: 2026:KHC-D:3426  MFA No. 101943 of 2018 HC-KAR  ORAL JUDGMENT
Challenging judgment and award dated 28.02.2018 passed by VII Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi sitting at Chikodi, ('Tribunal' for short) in MVC no.860/2016, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Sri SC Bhuti, learned counsel appearing for appellants submits that appeal is by NWKRTC being aggrieved by quantum of compensation in claim petition filed by respondent.

It was submitted as per claimant, on 23.12.2015 when claimant was going home on his bullock cart by side of road near Akol village driver of NWKRTC Bus bearing no.KA.27/F-223 drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed bullock cart causing accident.
Due to same, claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Despite treatment at Government Hospital, Nippani and Dr.Nirmale Hospital, Nippani he did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3426 HC-KAR 3.
Claiming compensation he filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('MV Act' for short) against NWKRTC.
4. On appearance, claim petition was opposed on all counts including negligence and quantum.
5. Based on pleadings, Tribunal framed issues and recorded evidence, wherein claimant and Dr.Mohan Kalekar deposed as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked Exs.P1 to P14.
Respondents-NWKRTC did not lead evidence.

sentences.text:
On consideration, Tribunal held accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of bus by its driver and claimant was entitled for compensation from NWKRTC as follows:
1 Pain and suffering Rs.40,000/- 2 Medicine and hospital charges Rs.48,850/- 3 Nourishment charges Rs.5,000/- 4 Attendant and conveyance Rs.5,000/- 5 Loss of income during treatment Rs.18,000/-
period 6 Loss of future income 1,78,200/- 7 Loss of amenities future Rs.30,000/-
unhappiness Total Rs.3,25,050/-
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3426 HC-KAR 7.
Aggrieved by quantum of compensation, appeal was filed.

It was firstly submitted, though claimant stated that he was 50 years of age, doing agriculture and earning Rs.5.00 lakhs per annum,
he did not substantiate same with specific material.
Though notional income for year 2015 was Rs.8,000/-, Tribunal erred in taking it as Rs.9,000/- and awarding excess compensation.

It was further submitted PW2 who had examined claimant for assessment of disability and issued Ex.P.12-disability certificate had assessed limb disability at 45% even though claimant had sustained fractures of left scapula and lower end of left radius, which was exaggerated.
Despite same, Tribunal considered excessive loss of earning capacity at 15%.
Even rate of interest awarded at 9% was excessive and called for modification.
On said ground sought for allowing appeal.
8. On other hand Sri Ashok A. Naik, learned counsel appearing for respondent-claimant opposed appeal.

It was submitted claimant had substantiated about his earning by production of Ex.P.13-record of rights, which showed that extent of 2 acres 1 gunta of his land was licenced to grow NC: 2026:KHC-D:3426 HC-KAR tobacco.
It was further submitted tough PW.2 had assessed permanent disability at 45%, tribunal had considered only 15% as loss of earning capacity.

However,
insofar as rate of interest, learned counsel agreed, no reasons were assigned.

9. Heard learned counsel, perused impugned judgment and award and certified copies of pleadings,
depositions and exhibits, made available by learned counsel for appellant.
10.

From above, and since only NWKRTC is in appeal for reduction of award, point that would arise for consideration is:
"Whether compensation awarded by the Tribunal calls for modification as prayed?
11.
Same is answered in negative for following reasons.

12. At outset indeed claimant pleaded that he was earning Rs.5.00 lakhs per annum from agriculture, but failed to produce records to substantiate same, he produced NC: 2026:KHC-D:3426 HC-KAR record of rights of his land as Ex.P.13, same shows that land was licenced to grow tobacco,
a commercial crop.

As same would establish, claimant as land holder, his earning cannot be assessed The Divisional Controller vs Shri Dattatray Bhau Naik on 4 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38764879/

sentences.text: 3 notionally

Even insofar as extent of loss of earning capacity, there is material to establish claimant sustained grievous injuries of fracture of left scapula and lower end of left radius with deformity on account of malunion.
PW-2 endorsed claimant suffering loss of earning capacity.
Ex.P.12-disability certificate indicates shortening of left limb by 1 inch with wasting of muscle and Grade-V muscle power.
Considering occupation as agriculturist, some difficulty or restriction in usage of left upper limb can be implied.
Consequently, assessment of loss of earning capacity at 15% cannot be stated to be without any basis or contrary to material on record.
14. Insofar as rate of interest, it is seen that tribunal has not assigned any specific reason.

Hence,
same liable to be reduced to 6%.
NC: 2026:KHC-D:3426 HC-KAR 15.
Consequently, point for consideration is answered partly in affirmative only insofar as reduction of interest from 9% to 6% per annum.
Except on interest portion, in all other respects, award is confirmed.

Hence following:
ORDER (i) Appeal is allowed in part, judgment and award dated 28.02.2018 passed by VII District and Sessions Judge, Belagavi sitting at Chikodi, in MVC no.860/2016 is modified, confirming assessment of compensation but with reduced rate of interest at 6%.
(ii) Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for payment.

Sd/-
(RAVI V.HOSMANI) JUDGE EM, CT:VP LIST NO.: 1 SL NO.: 25
